concept: Female aspiring 1990s cable-access interviewer. Improvised professional glamour, oversized thrifted power blazer, costume jewelry, safety pin tailoring, worn appointment book. Catherine O'Hara comic performance energy, original face rather than likeness.
prompt:
Create an ORIGINAL FEMALE CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET for Penny Chase, an aspiring 1990s local cable-access television interviewer in the illustrated music video Let the Phone Book Sing. Attached image is STYLE AND SHEET FORMAT ONLY: match its mature graphic-novel ink-and-paint, expressive caricature, nuanced faces, tactile fabric, strong tapered outlines and cream paper. Do not copy Belle's face, hair, physique or costume.
Penny is a woman around 50, lanky with narrow sloping shoulders disguised by comically broad shoulder pads. Long angular face, short slightly upturned nose, small pointed chin, wide expressive mouth, one eyebrow dramatically higher than the other; faint under-eye creases. Original character-actor face, characterful rather than conventionally glamorous. Performance energy: elaborate professional confidence barely covering desperate eagerness, a practiced television-host smile which can instantly turn into intense listening or delighted self-congratulation. Catherine O'Hara is a reference for comic acting energy ONLY; absolutely no recognizable celebrity likeness, no Moira Rose imitation.
She is improvising the successful media personality she wants to become, using bargain substitutes. Her meticulously teased honey-blonde swept-up hair has darker roots and a visible practical bobby pin at the back. Oversized dusty petrol-teal secondhand power blazer with huge shoulder pads, slightly too-long sleeves rolled neatly once, a single gaudy imitation-gold sunburst brooch. Underneath a shiny mustard/cream/black abstract patterned polyester blouse with a loose scarf tie trying to look like silk. Black tapered trousers slightly short, practical black low pumps. Large obviously plastic ivory pearl clip-on earrings and one oversized costume cocktail ring. A worn burgundy appointment organizer with a cheap ballpoint tucked into it, held in one hand like a producer's important dossier. Only a couple readable hints of improvisation: a modest safety pin gathering excess blazer fabric near waist in the three-quarter view, and a little rubbed gold finish on brooch. Clothes lovingly arranged, not filthy or pathetic. She is resourceful, theatrical and ambitious, not a victim; humor is the gap between polished presentation and improvised materials. Do not overload with gimmicks.
Composition landscape reference sheet: one complete full-body three-quarter standing figure on LEFT, head to shoes visible, chest lifted and chin up in an optimistic self-important presenter's pose, free hand making an elegant rehearsed introduction. On RIGHT three large consistent head/shoulder studies of the SAME woman: poised professional smile; listening with worried eyes while maintaining smile; sudden delighted raised-brow 'I've landed the interview!' reaction. Same hair, face, earrings, blazer and blouse in every view. Clear uncluttered cream background, no scene, no phone yet, no other characters, no text labels, no graphic panels. Warm dimensional painted skin, sophisticated detailed ink hatching, clear silhouette. Not a children's book, photorealism or 3D.
PROMPT LOCK: Mature graphic-novel ink-and-paint; distinct character silhouettes; quieter layered backdrops. Narrator addresses audience and is imperceptible to residents. Preserve approved identities, costumes and lyric timing.
